- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent history shows sustained upward trend.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast peaks sharply after a low, reduce peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If model consistently underestimates prices during high volatility periods, add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged price movements: if true outcome is >5% above forecast 2–3 days later, adjust forecast to reflect delayed reaction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent spikes: if last 5 days show sharp increases, reduce forecast by 3–7% to prevent momentum overestimation.
